deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a philosophical-psychological fragment from Riemann's Naturphilosophie notes. It continues the previous page, which ends with the question 'What corresponds to the bodily process in the case of the simple sensory representation [e.g. the representation of a red point]?'.

(1) Bracketed, pencil-marked draft. This bodily process comprises (1) spatially, the nerve process in the peripheral end of a primitive fibre; (2) temporally, a duration.

(2) Clean version.
- Our sensations are composed of simple elements. Each element is the mental ('geistige') expression of a bodily process that is bounded in space and time and has a definite spatial and temporal extent.
- The process comprises (a) spatially, the peripheral end of one primitive nerve fibre, and (b) a time interval of roughly 1/9 to 1/10 of a second.
- Within these bounds no further differences can be perceived. One receives a single total impression whose quality is influenced equally by all parts of the process. In modern terms this is a temporal integration window (temporal resolution or fusion threshold) of about 100–110 ms, and a spatial resolution limit set by one receptor or fibre.
- Every mental activity requires an expenditure of force, i.e. consumption of nutrients.

Hypothesis explaining these facts:
- In the nervous system, discrete bodily processes bounded in space and time take place. Their purpose is to bind external stimuli into a mental unity.
- When such a process ends, its bodily carrier is destroyed (dissolved) and its constituents are excreted from the organism.
- Its mental expression, which Riemann identifies with Herbart's 'einfache Vorstellung' (simple representation), enters the soul.

(3) The fact of memory leads to the further hypothesis that with each act of thought something permanent enters the soul. This permanent element can make itself known as such under special circumstances, but exerts no lasting influence on the phenomena. A marginal note, perhaps 'bis zu 4', refers ahead.

The only quantity on the page is the time constant of 1/9 to 1/10 s, i.e. about 0.10–0.11 s. No derivation is involved.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no computation.

Empirically, the 1/9–1/10 s figure is a reasonable 19th-century estimate of the duration of a 'psychological moment' (visual persistence and fusion). It is not a sharp constant, and modern values vary with modality (roughly 30–150 ms).
The claim that the material carrier of each mental act is destroyed and excreted is a speculative physiological hypothesis without justification. Modern neuroscience rejects it.

results.what: Sensations are composed of elementary units, each the mental expression of a spatially and temporally bounded nerve process: spatially the peripheral end of one primitive fibre, temporally about 1/9–1/10 s, within which no differences are perceived.
results.modern_name: Temporal integration window / 'psychological moment' / perceptual fusion threshold; receptive-field resolution limit
results.usually_credited_to: Persistence-of-vision estimates go back to Newton, Segner, Plateau and others; the 'psychological moment' is associated with von Baer (1860), Exner and later Stroud (1955).

results.what: Hypothesis that each act of thought deposits something permanent in the soul (memory traces), within a Herbart/Fechner framework of soul-elements.
results.usually_credited_to: Herbart (Vorstellungen), Fechner; the engram concept is credited to Semon (1904).

deep.surprise_reason: This is non-mathematical speculative psychology in the Herbart–Fechner tradition. Closely related wording ('mit jedem einfachen Denkact tritt etwas Bleibendes, Substantielles in unsere Seele ein') appears in the posthumously published 'Fragmente philosophischen Inhalts / Zur Psychologie und Metaphysik' in Riemann's Gesammelte Werke (ed. Weber–Dedekind). The page is a draft of known material.

checkable.asserts: The proposed duration window spans 1/90 s (about 11 ms) between 1/10 s and 1/9 s.
The elementary process lasts about 0.111 s to 0.100 s, i.e. roughly 100–111 ms.

transcription_corrections: The struck-through word before 'Dieser Process umfasst' is illegible; 'Derselbe' is plausible but uncertain.
The marginal note at the end, 'bis zu 4[?]', is faint and uncertain; it may be a cross-reference ('bis zu 4').

Otherwise the machine transcription agrees with the image as far as legible: 'Nervenprocess im peripherischen Ende einer Primitivfaser', '1/9 bis 1/10 einer Secunde', 'Herbart's einfache Vorstellung', 'mit jedem Denkact etwas Bleibendes'.
